newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keating says world should make room for China.
newsitem.headline: Keating says world should make room for China.

text.p: The world needs to make room for China on a political level, Australia's former prime minister Paul Keating said on Friday.

"China needs room to be made for it and deserves to be dealt with appropriately as a major world power as well as a regional power," he told the International Securities Market Association (ISMA) annual conference.
"Nationalism will replace communism as the glue that holds China together," he added.

"In the end, the direction China takes will be heavily shaped by whether the other major powers accept that China has a legitimate global role and provide the international space in which it can begin to exercise leadership in its own right," he said. Keating said there was growing suspicion of China, especially on the right in the United States.
"The reality is China is entirely focused on internal development," he said.
"A strong and successful China will sometimes be difficult for the rest of the world to deal with, but not as difficult as a weak and divided China," he added.
In Southeast Asia, Keating said the key to growth in Southeast Asia lay in Indonesia, the world's fourth most populous country.
But despite a doubling of per capita incomes every 10 years in the region, Keating said Southeast Asia faced challenges to growth.
"The increments to growth become harder to obtain as the base economy gets larger," Keating said.
"The Tiger economies are entering a new economic phase in which they need to innovate, add more value and move up the technology ladder -- less perspiration, more innovation," he said.
As economies continued to open up, increased political openness would follow, Keating said.
